parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Positronium is a system in which an electron and a positron orbit, with the same period around their common centre of mass, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The radius *r* of the orbit of both particles is 1.59 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
parts.text: Explain how the electric force between the electron and the positron causes the path of the moving particles to be circular.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the electric force between the electron and the positron is 2.28 × 10⁻⁹ N.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(ii) to determine the period of the circular orbit of the two particles.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Positronium is highly unstable, and after a very short period of time it becomes gamma radiation.
parts.text: Describe how gamma radiation is formed from the two particles in positronium.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State one medical application of the process described in (c)(i).

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: An electron and a positron orbit a marked centre of mass on a dashed circular path, with the radius labelled r.
